BM01.question: Does the candidate add a disease-relevant biological process not already represented by the panel?

options.label: Complementary process
options.definition: Adds a supported process relevant to the intended use and absent from the fixed panel roles.

options.label: Same underlying process
options.definition: Represents a process already captured by the fixed panel.

options.label: Process outside the intended use
options.definition: Supported role falls outside the specified biological use.

options.label: Mixed or context-dependent roles
options.definition: Relevant roles differ across contexts or include both represented and additional processes.

options.label: Insufficient evidence
options.definition: Decisive facts, identity, source coverage or usable context are missing. Do not interpret this as a negative finding.

BM02.question: Does the cited assay-validation experiment support use in the proposed specimen matrix?

options.label: Direct matrix evidence
options.definition: Validation directly tests the proposed specimen matrix.

options.label: Related matrix requiring validation
options.definition: Evidence tests a related matrix whose transfer still requires validation.

options.label: Different matrix only
options.definition: Available validation tests only a different matrix.

options.label: Conflicting matrix evidence
options.definition: Comparable matrix-validation records give incompatible findings.

options.label: Insufficient evidence
options.definition: Decisive facts, identity, source coverage or usable context are missing. Do not interpret this as a negative finding.

BM03.question: Does the study comparison address the intended clinical distinction?

options.label: Same clinical distinction
options.definition: Case, comparator and decision time match the intended distinction.

options.label: Healthy controls only
options.definition: Cases are compared only with healthy controls, without establishing the intended alternative condition.

options.label: Different clinical distinction
options.definition: The study contrasts different clinical states from the intended use.

options.label: Mixed comparison with unresolved subgroups
options.definition: Pooled comparisons do not resolve the required subgroups.

options.label: Insufficient evidence
options.definition: Decisive facts, identity, source coverage or usable context are missing. Do not interpret this as a negative finding.
